To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

polyphenolic compounds incorporated into the lipid phase of biological and model membranes change the packing order in the hydrophillic part of the lipid bilayer, which is reflected by the increase in the proportion of echinocyte erythrocytes.

the phenolic extracts of apple, chokeberry and strawberry incorporated into erythrocytes and liposomes changed their packing order, and this effect was the most pronounced for the apple extract, while the fluidity of the membrane was not affected.

polyphenolic compounds extracted from apple, chokeberries and strawberries affect the morphology of red blood cells and packing order in the hydrophillic phase of the erytrocyte membrane and liposomes formed of lipids from erythrocyte membranes and phosphatidycholine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
changes caused by polyphenolic extracts in the lipid phase in the model and biological membranes.
the effect of polyphenolic substances from fruits on the structure and properties of the membrane, which can be used in future to improve the therapeutic effect of polyphenols.
the effects of polyphenolic substances on the lipid phase of biological and model membranes, as well as their influence on the erythrocytes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
polyphenolic compounds incorporated into the lipid bilayers modify their structure, and thus their function.
the polyphenolic compounds affect the packing order of the lipid phase of biological and model membranes.
the studied phenolic extracts from fruits affect the lipid packing order in biological and model membranes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

polyphenolic compounds contained in fruit extracts are incorporated into the outer region (hydrophilic phase) of the lipid bilayer, changing the packing density in this region and the morphology of red blood cells.
the polyphenolic compounds contained in fruit extracts are able to modify the structure and properties of the membrane lipid bilayer, which can be of importance in the process of biological activity.
the phenolic extracts from the studied fruits are able to penetrate the outer region of erythrocytes and liposomes and to change the packing density of lipids.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the polyphenolic compounds contained in apple, chokeberry and strawberry extracts affect the erythrocytes and liposomes by changing their packing order, which may have an impact on the biological activity of these membranes.
the polyphenolic extracts affect the lipid phase of biological membranes and liposomes, which is important for understanding their biological activity.
the polyphenolic compounds in the extracts of the studied fruits can be incorporated into the lipid bilayer, affecting its properties.
